title: SR-1.30 Done holds across computers and clones
request: Closes G95: a contract's done state must mean the same on every computer and clone of a vault, and come only from a passing verify of the contract as signed. Split from SR-1.27 at its three-round stop (lead decision under the owner's delegation, 31 October 2026): SR-1.27 keeps task 1, which protects contracts/closed/ and contracts/receipts/ in every path form; this contract takes SR-1.27's task 2, the done state that comes from the verify record, with round 3's answers about pre-upgrade closes, close keys, swapped bodies, supersession and pulls. The stopgap #273 already refuses a key id that is not 16 hex, a signed body whose id is not the contract asked for, and a supersede that was not signed on this computer and passed. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-1.27, QL-1.02. Sensitive path (contracts and signatures): the QL-1.03 checklist applies before merge.

tasks.title: State comes from the verify record, not a file
requirements: a signed contract is done when the log holds a contract.verified record for its id with ok true and the signed hash, or when contracts/closed/<id>.json is a close record whose envelope has the close payloadType and verifies under this vault's own contract key or under a key committed to the vault's backup no later than the commit that adds the close, with a keyid of the 16-hex form, and whose verified payload holds exactly the keys id, hash, ok and verified_at, with id equal to the contract's id, ok true and hash equal to the signed hash; the fields are read from the verified payload, never from keys stored beside the envelope; a key placed on disk but never committed, or committed after the close, is not trusted for it, and no token can write contracts/keys/; any other file under contracts/closed/ plays no part in contractList, contractGate or the pre-push gate

done is a fact about a past verify: a later failing verify of a done contract is recorded and reported but does not reopen it, because a scope criterion can fail later for changes made after the work landed
memev doctor lists every contract whose contracts/closed/<id>.json exists but which is not done under requirement 1, as a contract to verify again; nothing is rewritten or deleted

a vault written by the code at the base, whose contracts were closed by a real passing verify, reads them as done after the change, and so does every other computer and clone of it: on open with the new code, each unsigned close whose contract has a counting pass in this vault's log is re-issued once as a signed close with this computer's key; an unsigned close with no such pass anywhere reads open everywhere and memev doctor names it

contractCheckSignature refuses any keyid that is not the 16-hex form keyId() produces, before the keyid touches a path, and accepts a signature only by the key whose keyid the contract.signed log record holds (or, with no such record, the keyid in <id>.sig.json, still 16-hex)

contract.verified records the canonical hash of contracts/signed/<id>.json as read and signature-checked by that verify, never a hash copied from the contract.signed record, and the keyid its signature verified under; the signed hash of a contract is the hash in this log's contract.signed record for its id or, with no such record (a clone, or a contract signed on another computer), the canonical hash of contracts/signed/<id>.json whose signature verifies under requirement 5; a verify counts toward done only when its hash equals the signed hash; a contract.verified record written before this change carries no hash and counts while the contract's signed files still verify under the keyid of its contract.signed record

verify writes contracts/closed/<id>.json as a close record: a DSSE envelope with its own payloadType, distinct from the contract signature's, over exactly {id, hash, ok: true, verified_at} with hash the signed hash, made with this computer's contract key, whose public file verify writes under contracts/keys/ when it is missing, so an honest close travels with the backup and verifies on every computer
the set of contracts with a counting pass survives a restart and an upgrade: it is rebuilt from the log on open or saved in graph.json with the snapshot's seq, never held only in memory
contractList and contractGate answer from that in-memory set, kept current by each contract.verified record, never from a log scan per call
with the daemon up, memev doctor relays the unverified-close check (the allow-list in doctor.mjs), and the check carries no fix: doctor --fix leaves the file and the log untouched

memev_contract_status with no arguments and the session-start card list a done contract whose latest verify failed as done, with the failing tasks of that verify, never as active work: the card says neither 'Active contract' nor 'Build these' for it, and such contracts do not count toward the card's limit of open contracts; memev gate verifies only contracts that are not done, so a done contract never blocks a push and gate appends no verify record for it

a supersedes link takes the superseded contract out of the open state, contractGate and the default status list only when the superseding contract was signed with local origin (decided by the transport, never by an argument), either in the superseded contract's session as the transport identifies it (the session of the caller's own connection, never a session argument) or by a caller with the admin scope, and has a counting pass of its own; until then the superseded contract stays open, in contractGate and in the default status list

contractSign validates a draft as contractDraft does, at least one task and no top-level key that contractDraft does not write, and refuses an id that already has a contract.signed record in this log, even when its signed files are gone from disk

docs/CONTRACTS.md says that a new version retires the old contract only when it was signed with local origin, in the old contract's session or by the owner and has passed a verify of its own, so an amend signed in a later session by a client without the admin scope leaves the old contract open until it passes
contractCheckSignature refuses a signed body whose id is not the id asked for, so a second contract's signed files copied over the first never verify as it

a close accepted from a file is recorded in the log the first time this vault sees it (a contract.close-accepted record with the close's hash and keyid), so a later pull that removes or replaces the file does not reopen the contract

a retirement is recorded as a signed envelope, contracts/retired/<old id>.json, over {old id, new id, the new contract's signed hash, the condition met: session or admin}, made with this computer's contract key under requirement 1's key rule and written only by the engine; every computer and clone decides supersession from that envelope, not from the signing vault's log

contracts/receipts/ merges as a union in git, like memory/ and work/, so two computers' verify entries both survive; a receipt pulled from another computer that keeps every entry this vault's log holds, in order, is accepted as it is, never restored and never imported as an external version

The device-shaped token writes contracts/drafts/x.json = {schema:'attest/1', title:'x', supersedes:A, tasks:[]} through MCP, signs it through MCP with no session, and verifies it if the sign succeeds (a contract with no tasks may be refused at signing). criteria.statement: T1-c21: Build A1 and A2 with the base code (git archive $MEMEV_CONTRACT_BASE as in T1-c09; skipped when unset, and the guard counts a skip as a failure) sharing a bare remote. On A1 sign A and K (session S); verify A PASS on A1; A2 syncs and verifies K PASS; both sync; give B on A1 a hand-placed closed file. Open both with the new code, sync A2 then A1, and open a fresh-.memev clone of the remote with the new code. A and K are done on A1 (K out of contractGate(S)), on A2 and in the clone; B is open everywhere; memev doctor names only B; memev gate --workdir <K's workdir> on A2 exits 0 and appends no contract.verified record. Red at base: B reads done.

criteria.statement: T1-c22: Two vaults A1 and A2 share a bare remote as in T1-c18. On A1 sign A (session S, only criterion false) and B (only criterion true) with A1's key; A2 syncs. On A2 copy B's signed and sig files over A's, verify A, restore A's files, close() and reopen A2. While B's body sits at A's path, contractCheckSignature(A) on A2 is not ok and no counting pass is recorded; after reopen A is open on A2; a fresh-.memev clone whose tree holds B's files at A's path reads A open and its doctor names A. Red at base: A2's verify closes A.

criteria.statement: Changes stay in scope

stop_rules: If any criterion fails after the fix: STOP, report the measured result, the failing check and file:line. Do not start the next task.
If the work needs a path outside scope: STOP and ask the owner to amend the contract. Never widen scope silently.
